scan_metadata.paper: Adaptive Linear Path Model-Based Diffusion (Shimizu & Tomizuka), arXiv 2602.02831
scan_metadata.explanation: All 61 tracked files were listed. The READMEs, all 8 entry scripts, the YAML configs and the implementation paths behind the selected commands were read; some controller internals (MPPI, Brax VP/MPPI/CEM/CMA-ES, ActorCritic.evaluate) were read only in outline. Seven documented commands are selected as execution sources and proposed as seven cli_wrapper tools (Figs. 3-6 and Tables I-II of the paper). RL fine-tuning (run_rl_fine_tuning.py) is deferred because of its training cost and because it overwrites the shipped checkpoint. Path generators and module __main__ self-tests are omitted as setup or internal code. No repository code was executed during the scan; all feasibility numbers are estimates unless they quote a workspace measurement.
scan_metadata.provenance_note: The paper's anonymous repository (anonymous.4open.science/r/adaptive_linear_path_model_based_diffusion-C58C) has expired (HTTP 410). This public repository by the first author has the same name and is used instead. It is not established that it is byte-identical to the paper's artifact.
scan_metadata.licence_note: The repository has NO licence file (no LICENSE/COPYING among the 61 tracked files at the pinned commit). Redistribution of its code, checkpoint and figures inside a delivered package is not covered by any licence. The coordinator should record this in USAGE.md and decide whether the ZIP references the checkout instead of bundling it.

tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: Documented command. It reproduces the paper's Fig. 3 (one row per --name). The figure is the only output, and the shipped reference images make it verifiable.

tutorials.title: Path tracking with MPPI / VP-MBD / LP-MBD (paper Table II, VP-MBD and LP-MBD rows)
tutorials.description: From the vehicle_control directory: python run_experiment.py --config config/{mppi,vp_mbd,lp_mbd}_controller.yaml [--seed N] [--device cuda|cpu] [--save_mode True]. Runs one episode of the kinematic-vehicle path-tracking environment and prints the episode reward, the episode length and the average solve time per control step [ms]. tutorials.title: ALP-MBD with the shipped PPO tuner: per-step (T, sigma_max) along the path (paper Figs. 5 and 6)

tutorials.title: PPO training of the ALP-MBD scheduler (paper Sec. IV-B, Algorithm 1)
tutorials.description: python run_rl_fine_tuning.py --config config/lp_mbd_fine_tuning.yaml [--disable_wandb] [--seed] [--device]. Trains the PPO tuner for max_training_steps=1,000,000 control steps and saves it to <script_dir>/data/fine_tuner_checkpoints/lp_mbd_fine_tuner.pth.
tutorials.reason_for_include_or_exclude: DEFERRED. 1e6 LP-MBD control steps at the documented setting would take about 10-13 h even at the paper's RTX 4090 per-step latency (37-45 ms), and days on CPU. Training length is a YAML key only (no CLI flag). The script overwrites the shipped checkpoint in the source tree unless run on a copy. The result is stochastic, and the paper prints no training curve to compare against. The shipped checkpoint already supports the evaluation tool.

tool_review.ownership: All exposed tools belong to one module, src/tools/cli_wrapper.py (one implementer, one separate verifier). Every tool invokes the original script with sys.executable, an argument list and shell=False.
general_wrapping_requirements: OUTPUTS ARE WRITTEN INTO THE SOURCE TREE. tutorial/plot_utils.py saves to dirname(__file__)/images/{1d,2d}. run_rl_evaluation.py saves to <script_dir>/video/ and reads <script_dir>/data/.... run_experiment.py writes the GIF to <cwd>/video/. run_rl_fine_tuning.py overwrites <script_dir>/data/fine_tuner_checkpoints/lp_mbd_fine_tuner.pth. Running in place would overwrite the committed reference figures. Every call (executor or wrapper) should therefore run an unmodified per-call copy of the relevant directory (tutorial/ or vehicle_control/, about 1.1 MB without .git) inside the call's output directory, check that the copied .py/.yaml/.pth hashes equal the pinned ones, and use that copy as cwd. Do not edit upstream files.

Parameters that only exist as YAML keys (ref_path, render, diffusion_steps, ...) are changed in a per-call config copy written next to the copied scripts. These keys are documented in vehicle_control/README.md. run_experiment.py applies YAML keys with setattr after argparse, so a YAML key overrides a CLI flag with the same name. Do not put seed/device/save_mode into the YAML copy.

Headless use: MPLBACKEND=Agg makes every plt.show() return immediately with a 'FigureCanvasAgg is non-interactive' UserWarning. env.render(mode='human') calls plt.pause(0.001) and plt.cla() on every control step, which draws off-screen and saves nothing. For metric-only runs, set render: False in the config copy. This does not affect control or metrics. For a GIF, set render: True and pass --save_mode True.
--save_mode is declared type=bool in all three vehicle_control scripts, so any non-empty string (including 'False') becomes True. Pass the literal 'True' to enable it and omit the flag otherwise.

Device: the tutorial scripts have no device flag and use CUDA whenever torch.cuda.is_available(). With a CUDA build of torch, force CPU through the environment (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=''). vehicle_control scripts take --device cuda|cpu (default cuda, falls back to cpu if CUDA is unavailable). CPU and GPU use different RNG streams, so numbers and figures differ between devices even with fixed seeds.

torch.compile: vehicle_control/envs/pathtracking.py (normalize_angle, step, _calc_closest_ref_idx, _calc_lateral_offset) and controller/{lp,vp}_mbd_controller.py (reverse_once, _states_prediction) are decorated with @torch.compile. The first call compiles with Inductor, which needs a C++ compiler on CPU (gcc/g++ are present at /usr/bin) plus Python headers, and Triton on CUDA. Changing diffusion_steps (every step in run_rl_evaluation) can trigger recompiles up to Dynamo's cache limit. Compile time and memory are unmeasured, so executors should record them. Setting TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR inside the project avoids sharing /tmp/torchinductor_<user>.
Capture stdout/stderr and the exit status. All scientific results of the vehicle and Brax commands are stdout lines. Parse only the lines quoted per tool below.

candidates.task_and_io: Run one closed-loop path-tracking episode (kinematic vehicle, static 10x10 m obstacle at reference row 300) with MPPI, VP-MBD or LP-MBD and report tracking reward and per-step solve time. Proposed inputs: controller in {mppi, vp_mbd, lp_mbd} (selects config/<controller>_controller.yaml); reference_path in {s_bend (config default), oval, straight}, or a user CSV (header line, columns x,y,yaw,v; at least 302 rows because PathTrackingEnv.reset hard-codes the obstacle at row 300 and reads obstacles[0]); seed (int, default 0); device (cuda|cpu); save_gif (bool). Optional documented YAML keys: diffusion_steps, sigma_max (lp), beta0/beta1 (vp), temperature, num_samples, horizon, max_episode_length. The implementer chooses a minimal tested subset. Outputs (stdout): 'episode reward: <tensor>', 'episode length: <int>', 'average solve time: <float>  [ms]', 'average episode reward: <float>', 'average episode length: <float>', plus 'Goal reached' / 'Collision detected' events. With save_gif: <cwd>/video/seed_<seed>_<filename> (filename from the YAML, e.g. lp_mbd_controller.gif).
candidates.implementation: vehicle_control/run_experiment.py:main, which uses envs/pathtracking.py:PathTrackingEnv, controller/{mppi_controller.MPPI, vp_mbd_controller.VPMBDController, lp_mbd_controller.LPMBDController} and utils/evaluate.py:evaluate(eval_num=1). ref_path = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), cfg.ref_path); an absolute ref_path in the config copy also works because of os.path.join semantics.
candidates.command: cd <copy of vehicle_control>; <PROJECT_PYTHON> run_experiment.py --config <copy>/config/<controller>_controller.yaml(or edited copy) --seed <n> --device <dev> [--save_mode True]
candidates.paper_mapping: Table II VP-MBD row (T=17, beta 1e-4/1e-2; reward -3498 +/- 116, 38.3 ms) and LP-MBD row (T=17, sigma_max 1.8; reward -3465 +/- 147, 36.9 ms). Table II reports means over five seeds on an RTX 4090; the seed values are not stated (0-4 is the natural reading). The MPPI config is a repository baseline that is not in Table II.
candidates.verification_source: No shipped metric logs. Reference = a standalone run of the same command (seed 0 at least; 5 seeds for a Table II comparison if time allows). Compare the parsed reward and length exactly on repeat runs (same device; LP-MBD reseeds a torch.Generator every control step, VP/MPPI use the global seed) and the reward order of magnitude against Table II. Runtime is hardware-dependent. vehicle_control/video/seed_0_mbd_controller.gif (55b9c41e...) shows an oval-path run, but no current config produces that filename (all configs use s_bend and other filenames), so it is not a reproducible reference.
candidates.feasibility: s-bend reference: 942 points at 0.2 m spacing (about 188 m) at 5 m/s, so an episode is a few hundred control steps (ends at goal within 1 m, collision, or max_episode_length=1000). Per step: diffusion_steps-1 = 16 reverse passes x 100 samples x 50-step rollouts. GPU at the paper's latency is about 37 ms/step, i.e. under a minute plus compile. CPU is unmeasured, probably minutes per episode plus torch.compile time. MEMORY HOTSPOT: utils/path_utils.py:calc_longitudinal_offset_to_segment computes torch.diag(segment_vec @ target_vec.T) over num_samples*horizon points. That is 5000x5000 float32 = 100 MB per cost call at the defaults and grows quadratically (10000 gives 400 MB, 20000 gives 1.6 GB), so cap num_samples*horizon if those keys are exposed. With save_gif, every frame (640x480 ARGB, about 1.2 MB) is held in memory until the end, about 0.5 GB for 400 steps, plus the moviepy write.
candidates.headless: All three shipped configs have render: True. Without --save_mode, every step calls plt.pause/plt.cla under Agg (wasted drawing, no file). Use render: False in the copy for metric runs.
candidates.notes: The GIF frames are ARGB bytes (canvas.tostring_argb) passed to moviepy as RGB(A), and the shipped GIF shows channel-shifted colours (black path drawn red). This is upstream behaviour. tostring_argb exists in matplotlib 3.9.0, 3.10.x and 3.11.2 (checked in local installs).

candidates.headless: The evaluation config has render: True, so every step calls plt.pause/plt.cla. Set render: False in the copy; the final figure does not depend on it. plt.show() after savefig is harmless under Agg.
candidates.caveat: utils/evaluate.py:evaluate_single_episode appends episode_reward and episode_length inside the step loop (lines 202-203). The printed 'average episode reward/length' are therefore means of running partial sums, not episode totals, and are not comparable with Table II rewards. Report them only as raw stdout, or not at all.

candidates.task_and_io: Receding-horizon control of a Brax task with LP-MBD, VP-MBD, MPPI, CEM or CMA-ES, reporting the mean per-step reward over seeds 0-4. Inputs: env_name in {ant, hopper, halfcheetah, walker2d, reacher, pusher, inverted_double_pendulum, inverted_pendulum}; controller in {lp_mbd, vp_mbd, mppi, cem, cma_es}; horizon (int, default 50); sample_size (int, default 2000); total_diffusion_steps (int, default 50). The wrapper always passes --disable_wandb (otherwise wandb.init(mode='online') needs a W&B login and network). Outputs (stdout only): 'Seed <k> Average reward: <float>' x5, 'Final Average reward: <float>', 'Final Reward std: <float>' (std of the 5 per-seed means, as in Table I). No files.
candidates.implementation: brax_evaluation/main.py:main uses brax.envs.get_environment(env_name, backend='positional') and jax.jit(env.step/reset), with controllers/{lp_mbd.LPMBD, vp_mbd.VPMBD, mppi.MPPI, cem.CEM, cma_es.CMAES}; CEM and CMA-ES subclass MPPI. Each controller call runs total_diffusion_steps-1 jitted reverse_once steps with jax.vmap over sample_size and lax.scan over horizon.

candidates.hard_coded_settings: 5 seeds (0-4), total_env_steps=50 per seed, lam=0.1, backend 'positional'. LP-MBD sigma_max=2.0 (controllers/lp_mbd.py:37; the paper text says 1.8). VP beta0=1e-4, betaT=1e-2. None of these is exposed on the CLI.
candidates.paper_mapping: Table I (Ant, Hopper, HalfCheetah, Walker2D, Reacher, Pusher x CEM, MPPI, VP-MBD, LP-MBD; mean +/- std over 5 seeds). The paper does not state the T/H/N used ('same for all'). README defaults are 50/50/2000. cma_es and the two pendulum tasks are extra.
candidates.verification_source: Standalone run of the same reduced command; repeat-run equality (fixed PRNGKey seeds). The Table I magnitude is only loosely comparable at reduced sizes.
candidates.feasibility: Blocked: HEAVY_JOBS_DISABLED is set, so heavy.sh refuses with exit 75. Default size is 5 x 50 x 49 x 2000 x 50 = about 1.2e9 simulated env steps per call; for comparison the workspace MBD hopper measurement (about 1e7 env steps) took about 1.2 GB and 4 minutes, so defaults would take hours and are infeasible. The problem-size knobs are --sample_size (memory scales with it through vmap), --horizon and --total_diffusion_steps (time); seeds and env steps cannot be reduced. Suggested reference run: --env_name hopper (or inverted_pendulum) --controller lp_mbd --sample_size 128 --horizon 20 --total_diffusion_steps 10 --disable_wandb, about 5 x 50 x 9 x 128 x 20 = 5.8e6 env steps, expected well within 2.5 GB and a few minutes plus JIT compile (unmeasured). Record the reduction exactly. Use --limit-mb 2500 and a timeout.
candidates.headless: No plotting. tqdm progress goes to stderr.

candidates.task_and_io: Train the PPO scheduler (Algorithm 1) on the s-bend path and save a new tuner checkpoint.
candidates.implementation: vehicle_control/run_rl_fine_tuning.py:main uses PPOTuner.select_action/update/save, PPOBuffer and evaluate(agent=...) every 30 episodes. It saves to os.path.join(<script_dir>, fine_tuner_model_path).
candidates.blocker: Documented setting max_training_steps=1,000,000 (YAML only; no CLI flag), with a PPO update every 2*max_episode_length=2000 steps and K_epochs=40. At the paper's 37-45 ms/step this is about 10-13 h on an RTX 4090 and days on CPU. It overwrites the shipped checkpoint unless run on a copy. It imports wandb at module level (needs --disable_wandb for offline use). It is stochastic, and the paper has no training curve to compare. A bounded smoke run (e.g. max_training_steps 2000 = one PPO update) would be possible through a config copy, but it would not reproduce a paper result. Add it only on request.

doc_code_discrepancies: tutorial/run_1d_example.py:39 sets VP beta1=0.1 (comment '# 1e-2'). The paper (Sec. V intro, Eq. (20): VP std [0.1, 0.01] for T=2 and 0.16 for T=5) corresponds to beta1=0.01. The shipped gaussian_results_1d.png VP panel differs visibly from paper Fig. 3 (middle row). The run uses the code value.
brax_evaluation/controllers/lp_mbd.py:37 hard-codes sigma_max=2.0. The paper says sigma_max=1.8 for LP-MBD 'throughout this experiment'.

vehicle_control/README.md section 5 says fine_tuner_model_path must point to an existing checkpoint. run_rl_evaluation.py ignores that key and always loads <script_dir>/data/fine_tuner_checkpoints/<policy>_fine_tuner.pth.
utils/evaluate.py:evaluate_single_episode averages running partial sums (append inside the loop), so the printed 'average episode reward' is not an episode reward.
--save_mode type=bool in run_experiment.py, run_rl_fine_tuning.py and run_rl_evaluation.py: '--save_mode False' enables GIF saving.
tutorial/alp_mbd.py samples sigma_max with relu but reports the optimum with softplus.
Paper Fig. 4 caption calls the top row 'VP-MBD'. Both code and figure plot AVP-MBD (learned beta) in that row, labelled 'VP'.
brax_evaluation/main.py argparse choices list reacher and pusher twice (harmless).
generate_oval_path.py writes data/oval_path.csv and generate_straight_path.py writes data/straight_path.csv, while the shipped and used CSVs are under data/path/.

execution_plan_hints: Run executors serially or at most two light ones at a time. About 2.6 GB was available at scan time and VS Code holds several GB.

Tutorial executors: copy tutorial/*.py into the executor namespace, run each documented --name (3 + 4) plus run_alp_mbd.py and run_avp_mbd.py, keep the PNGs and stdout, and compare with the shipped PNGs.

vehicle_control executors: copy vehicle_control/ (scripts, config/, data/), set render: False in config copies, run run_experiment.py for lp_mbd and vp_mbd (seed 0 at least; mppi optional), and run run_rl_evaluation.py for oval and s_bend. Record torch.compile time, wall time per episode, peak RSS, and the device used.
Brax executor: only if HEAVY_JOBS_DISABLED is removed, run through heavy.sh with the reduced arguments; otherwise report 'not attempted'.
